title: The day a wave of syrup hit Boston 🌊
subject: molasses
description:
Did you know about this one? 👇

The Great Molasses Flood of January 15, 1919: a storage tank burst in Boston's North End, releasing 2.3 million gallons of molasses. Here's why the cold made it so deadly.

Sources: Smithsonian Magazine, TIME, NBC News
tags: why was the molasses flood deadly

scenes.text: A wave of syrup taller than a house hit Boston.
January 15, 1919. A tank holding 2.3 million gallons of molasses burst open.
The wave tore through the North End at about 35 miles per hour.
But here's the strange part. The cold made it deadlier. In the winter air, the molasses thickened, and people who fell couldn't get up.
21 people died and about 150 were hurt. The tank's steel was far too thin.
